channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Fed’s Cook says inflation has stayed too high for too long
item.description: The Fed Governor Lisa Cook crossed the wires on Wednesday and said she is committed to returning inflation to the Fed’s 2% goal while preserving the strength of the labour market.

item.title: Mexican Peso pain deepens above 18.00 as carry appeal fades
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) prolongs its agony, extending losses by over 0.11% against the Greenback for the third straight day on Wednesday, while USD/MXN continues to trade above the psychological level of 18.00 as the carry trade loses its appeal.

item.title: Forex Today: Fedspeak, Jobless Claims and ISM data steal the show
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has traded with marginal gains, coming under pressure following daily tops near 101.50 as investors evaluated softer-than-expected PCE data in August and trimmed some bets on extra tightening by the Federal Reserve (Fed) in the following months.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Monthly outlook mixed, daily chart remains bearish
item.description: EUR/USD remains on the defensive on Wednesday as a broadly stronger US Dollar (USD) weighs on the pair, leaving the Euro on track for a loss of more than 2% in September. At the time of writing, EUR/USD trades around 1.1337, close to Tuesday’s low of 1.1312, its weakest level since May 2025.

item.title: Gold can’t catch a PCE break as long US yields keep climbing
item.description: Gold prices (XAU/USD) retreated on Wednesday, down 0.6%, after US inflation data came in above the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) 2% goal but below estimates, prompting investors to price in a less hawkish central bank than expected. The XAU/USD trades at $4,155 at the time of writing.

item.title: WTI set for monthly gain amid US-Iran stalemate
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil rebounds on Wednesday and remains on track for a monthly gain of around 5.5%. The lack of progress in US-Iran negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz keeps geopolitical risks elevated, even as Middle East supply conditions improve.

item.title: ECB’s Lagarde warns France needs a credible path to rein in debt
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde said that France’s debt situation is “serious at 120% of GDP and without a path to lowering it.”

item.title: ECB’s Schnabel says yields surge could cool inflation pressures
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member Isabel Schnabel said Wednesday that high costs are passed through to consumers more quickly when the economy is resilient.

item.title: Australian Dollar reverses post-PCE rebound as US Dollar recovers
item.description: AUD/USD declines 0.41% on Wednesday and trades around 0.6960 at the time of writing, having fully erased its initial rebound following the release of softer-than-expected United States (US) inflation data.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD remains vulnerable near $60
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades under pressure on Wednesday even as traders reduce bets that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates again in October following softer-than-expected US PCE inflation data.

item.title: British Pound catches second wind as soft PCE knocks Fed hike bets
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) posts solid gains versus the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, edging up 0.42% as the latest US inflation figures were below estimates, reaffirming New York Federal Reserve (Fed) President John Williams' comments that the Fed is in no rush to tighten monetary policy.

item.title: Gold loses momentum as the initial reaction to softer US PCE inflation fades
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) reverses its earlier gains on Wednesday after briefly climbing above $4,200 in reaction to softer-than-expected US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data. The initial move fades as the US Dollar (USD) trims its losses and US Treasury yields resume their advance.

item.title: China: Targeted support and cautious stabilization signs – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts note China has unveiled targeted support measures, including a 25bp cut to the PBoC’s PSL rate and expanded relending quotas for innovation, technology, agriculture and small businesses.

item.title: EUR/USD: Measured ECB tightening to support Euro – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities' Macro Research team expects the European Central Bank (ECB) to continue a measured tightening cycle, delivering a final 25bp hike in December and taking the deposit rate to 2.75%, which they see as mildly restrictive.

item.title: Japanese Yen advances as US PCE shifts Fed rate hike bets toward December
item.description: USD/JPY falls 0.30% on Wednesday and trades around 156.80 at the time of writing, as the US Dollar (USD) comes under selling pressure following softer-than-expected United States (US) inflation data.

item.title: Euro finds support as softer US PCE data prompts traders to trim Fed rate-hike bets
item.description: EUR/USD holds modest gains on Wednesday as traders assess the latest economic data from both sides of the Atlantic. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1363, up 0.20% on the day, after touching 1.1312 on Tuesday, its lowest level since May 2025.

item.title: China: PMIs point to manufacturing and services improvement – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Early Morning Reid notes that China’s latest PMI data show a broad-based pickup in activity. The private-sector RatingDog Manufacturing PMI and official manufacturing PMI both strengthened, with the latter returning to expansion. Services and non-manufacturing indices also improved, lifting the composite PMI above 50 and signaling a more supportive backdrop for Chinese equities and growth.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains as US inflation cools Fed October rate hike bets
item.description: USD/CAD declines 0.08% on Wednesday and trades around 1.4180 at the time of writing, after touching a daily low of 1.4155 in the wake of US inflation data. The pair recovered some losses as investors reassessed the timing of a potential further tightening by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: EUR/GBP: Range set to persist – Rabobank
item.description: RaboResearch Global Economics & Markets’ FX Strategy team assesses EUR/GBP in light of UK politics, growth and monetary policy. They note the Pound’s recent support from stronger UK GDP, but expect GBP bulls to stay cautious ahead of the October 28 budget.

item.title: Euro: France fiscal risks to have limited drag – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad reports EUR/USD has stabilized after dropping to its lowest level since May 2025, as widening France-Germany yield spreads highlight growing French fiscal concerns.

item.title: Breaking: US core PCE inflation stays unchanged at 3% in August vs. 3.3% expected
item.description: Annual inflation in the United States (US), as measured by the change in the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, held steady at 3.4% in August, the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported on Wednesday.

item.title: British Pound rebounds against Japanese Yen as UK growth beats expectations
item.description: GBP/JPY rebounds sharply on Wednesday as the British Pound (GBP) strengthens across the board following an upward revision to UK economic growth. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 208.65 after recovering from 206.89 earlier in Asian trading hours, the lowest since December 2025.

item.title: Breaking: United States private sector employment rises by 90K in September vs. 70K expected
item.description: Employment in the United States' (US) private sector increased by 90K in September, the Automatic Data Processing (ADP) reported on Wednesday. This reading followed the 36K increase recorded in August (revised from 38K) and came in better than the market expectation of 70K.

item.title: Germany annual CPI inflation rises to 3.3% in September
item.description: Inflation in Germany, as measured by the change in the Consumer Price Index, climbed to 3.3% (preliminary) in September from 2.9% in August, Germany's Destatis reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Indian Rupee recovers as traders trim hawkish Fed bets, oil prices fall
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains against the US Dollar (USD) after a flat opening on Wednesday.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Reaching oversold levels at six-week lows sub-0.8550
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is dropping sharply against the British Pound (GBP) on Wednesday, as UK data has endorsed recent claims by Bank of England (BoE) officials to hike interest rates, while German data disappointed on Wednesday.

item.title: What is driving the US Dollar to multi-month highs against the Euro as PCE data approaches?
item.description: EUR/USD has dropped to its lowest level since mid-2025 as the US Dollar (USD) maintains broad-based momentum, propelled by elevated long-dated US Treasury yields and shifting expectations for Federal Reserve (Fed) monetary policy.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: At make or a break near 1.1330
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is up 0.13% at around 1.1356 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Softer CPI keeps RBA pricing in check – BBH
item.description: Elias Haddad at Brown Brothers Harriman notes the Australian Dollar is underperforming after a softer August CPI print weighed on RBA cash rate futures. Headline CPI rose less than consensus, while trimmed mean inflation remained steady for a third month.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal tightening risks dovish BOE repricing – BBH
item.description: BBH’s Elias Haddad highlights that Pound gains were supported by an upward revision to UK Q2 GDP, with growth beating both prior estimates and Bank of England (BOE) forecasts.
